stories.headline: Karnataka will always be there for its neighbours, Shivakumar tells Naidu after cyclone help
stories.title: Karnataka will always be there for its neighbours, Shivakumar tells Naidu after cyclone help
stories.summary: Responding to Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu’s letter of thanks for help in restoring power after Cyclones Arnab and Murasu, D.K. Shivakumar says his State will always stand by its neighbours
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar has reaffirmed his State’s commitment to inter-State solidarity, saying that Karnataka was glad to extend a helping hand to neighbouring Andhra Pradesh in restoring electricity following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu.

Responding to a formal letter of appreciation from Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu, he said the support went beyond mere administrative aid, adding that neighbours stand by each other, especially in times of adversity.
“For us, this was never just about extending assistance; it was about standing together for people.

We will always be there for our neighbours, just as we know they would be there for us,” the Karnataka Chief Minister said, according to a press release from the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister’s Office.

Mr. Shivakumar’s remarks came in reply to a detailed letter from Mr. Naidu, who conveyed the heartfelt gratitude of the Andhra Pradesh government and its people for Karnataka's prompt mobilisation of manpower.
Following severe infrastructure damage caused by Cyclones Arnab and Murasu, Karnataka deployed 68 batches, comprising 592 personnel, to work alongside local teams under difficult field conditions.

In his letter, Mr. Naidu outlined the scale of the restoration challenge within the Andhra Pradesh Central Power Distribution Corporation Limited (APCPDCL) limits alone, where power supply had to be restored in 1,333 villages and 1,852 poles had been damaged after Cyclone Arnab, and in 1,825 villages with 7,850 damaged poles following Cyclone Murasu.

Alongside Karnataka's contingent, APCPDCL had deployed 165 batches, comprising 1,580 personnel, after Arnab and 390 batches, comprising 3,292 personnel, after Murasu to execute the restoration works on a war footing.

Noting that the two neighbouring States share close geographical, economic and cultural ties, Mr. Naidu said that cooperation during extreme weather events strengthens these bonds and helps build more resilient disaster response mechanisms.

Reciprocating the goodwill, the Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister assured Mr. Shivakumar that his government remains equally committed to mutual support and stands ready to deploy personnel, equipment, and machinery to Karnataka in the event of any natural calamity or emergency.

stories.title: Cyclone Akvan impact: Bengal set for heavy rain, ports sound warning
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: With Cyclone Akvan expected to make landfall along the Andhra Pradesh-Odisha coast on Friday, several districts of West Bengal are likely to receive rain and thunderstorms through the week, with isolated pockets facing heavy to very heavy showers.
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an orange alert for East and West Midnapore for Friday, forecasting 7-20 cm of rainfall in isolated areas.
The Regional Meteorological Centre, Kolkata, has warned that these two districts will receive heavy to very heavy rain of 7-20 cm in isolated pockets.
East Midnapore is also set to experience thunderstorms, lightning, and gusty winds of 40-50 kmph.

The weather bureau has also warned of possible lightning strikes in open fields, temporary waterlogging in low-lying areas and underpass roads on Thursday and Friday, damage to standing crops and horticulture, and damage to vulnerable kutcha houses, with the possibility of wall collapse.
With squally winds of up to 70 kmph and rough sea conditions forecast for Thursday, the weather bureau has advised fishermen not to venture into the deep sea until Friday.
Those already at sea have been asked to return to shore.
Meanwhile, Kolkata and Haldia ports have upgraded their alerts from a Distant Caution Signal to Distant Warning Signal No. 2, indicating a cyclone at sea and warning vessels preparing to leave port.
Sagar Island Port has also issued a corresponding storm warning.
It has advised people to seek shelter in safe places during thunderstorms and lightning, and avoid taking refuge under trees or near electric poles.
They have also been cautioned against contact with water bodies.

stories.headline: Delhi High Court Seeks Response Of ED, SFIO On Tina Ambani's Plea Seeking Disclosure Of LOC
stories.title: Delhi High Court Seeks Response Of ED, SFIO On Tina Ambani's Plea Seeking Disclosure Of LOC
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The Delhi High Court on Thursday issued notice on a plea filed by Tina.

A. Ambani, wife of industrialist Anil Ambani, seeking disclosure of whether any Look-Out Circular (LOC) has been issued against her by investigating agencies, including the Serious Fraud Investigation Office (SFIO) and the Enforcement Directorate (ED).
Justice Mini Pushkarna sought response of Bureau of Immigration, ED and SFIO while listing the matter on December 08.
Ambani has also sought suspension of any such LOC, if issued against her, to enable her to travel to Thailand, the United Arab Emirates, Oman and Bhutan between December 10 and December 30.

She has sought directions to the Bureau of Immigration and the investigating agencies to disclose the existence and particulars of any LOC against her, including its copy, the originating agency, the case or proceeding in which it was opened, the date of issuance, reference number, grounds recorded and present status.

Advocate Arshdeep Singh Khurana appearing for Ambani submitted that she wants to travel abroad to visit her family and friends and therefore, wants to know if any travel restrictions have been imposed against her.
He said that though the two agencies had summoned her, there are no pending summons as of now and that she has not been called any further.
“I wish to travel from December 10 to visit my family.
This is a disclosure petition that if there is an LOC, they may tell me and if there is no LOC, then it may come on record,” he said.
Appearing for ED, Senior Advocate Zoheb Hossain said that two summons were issued to Ambani however she did not appear in response to either of them.

As he sought time to file a short response to the plea, Khurana told Court that Ambani had communicated to the agency her willingness to appear but was suffering from a spinal fracture at the relevant time.
He said that after her intimation, no further summons have been issued to her.

stories.title: Infantino, Diallo, Tashima proposed for 2027 FIFA presidential election
stories.summary: Gianni Infantino is among three candidates proposed for the 2027 FIFA presidential election, which will take place in Rabat, Morocco, on March 18.
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Philippe Diallo, Gianni Infantino and Kohzo Tashima have been proposed as candidates for the FIFA presidential election scheduled to take place at the 77th FIFA Congress in Rabat, Morocco, on March 18, 2027.
FIFA confirmed on Thursday that its general secretariat had received the three candidatures from member associations following the call for election issued by the FIFA Council on April 29, 2026.
The names have been forwarded to FIFA’s electoral committee, which will examine the candidatures and decide on the admission of the candidates in accordance with the FIFA Governance Regulations.

Taking to the social media platform X, PM Modi wrote, "Paying tribute to former Prime Minister Smt. Indira Gandhi Ji on her birth anniversary." Indira Gandhi, popularly known as the 'Iron Lady of India', was born on November 19, 1917, in Allahabad, Uttar Pradesh, into a Kashmiri Pandit family. She was the daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru, India's first Prime Minister, and Kamala Nehru. She served as the Prime Minister from 1966 to 1977 and again from January 1980 until her assassination in 1984. She became a member of the Rajya Sabha in August 1964 and served until February 1967. Subsequently, she was elected to the Lok Sabha and remained a member during its fourth, fifth and sixth terms. Her role in the conflict established her reputation as a decisive leader with strong political resolve. National Integration Day is observed annually on November 19 to mark her birth anniversary and commemorate her contributions to national unity and integration. Throughout her political career, Gandhi emphasised the importance of bringing together people from diverse regions, cultures and communities under a common national identity. Her policies and political approach focused on strengthening India's unity and advancing its development. article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Tuesday (November 17) rejected plea filed by the Uttar Pradesh government and Uttar Pradesh Avas Evam Vikas Parishad (Housing Board) challenging an Allahabad High Court judgment that had set aside a demand of Rs 388 crore raised against real estate developer M/s Gaursons India Pvt.
A bench of Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe upheld the High Court's decision to quash the Chief Secretary's June 2022 order and the consequential demand notice of September 2022.
The matter pertains to land of Gaursons' predecessors-in-interest, which the Housing Board acquired for its Vasundhara Scheme in Ghaziabad.

In 1995, the Supreme Court disposed of the Housing Board's appeal on a compromise under which the acquired land (12.047 acres) would be adjusted in the scheme, to be used for water purification-related construction with the rest kept open, and no party would pay any value or compensation for the exchange.
In a 2004 Exchange Deed, two parcels (Khasra Nos. 948 and 1454) in Arthala village were allotted to the predecessors-in-interest which were sold to Gaursons in 2005.
It later emerged that the land had already been resumed by the District Magistrate in 1994 for a bird sanctuary.
After years of litigation, the Housing Board executed a second Exchange Deed in 2016, giving Gaursons alternative land in the Siddharth Vihar Yojana.
Gaursons had paid Rs 32.45 crore as land conversion charges.
It built 2,476 general houses and 450 EWS/LIG houses on the land, which were sold to homebuyers.

After a PIL in the High Court and a Special Investigation Team (SIT) report, the Chief Secretary's order of June 2022 directed that the land be allotted to Gaursons at the current bulk sale rate subsequent to which the Housing Board issued the Rs 388 crore demand notice.
The High Court set aside two conditions (ii & iii) of the order and the demand notice.
Thereafter, an appeal was filed before the Supreme Court.

New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismissed the Enforcement Directorate's (ED) petition challenging the interim bail granted to Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan by the Allahabad High Court in a money laundering case.
A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale declined to interfere with the High Court's November 17 order, noting that the relief granted to Khan was only interim bail.
The Supreme Court also clarified that the High Court's observations were prima facie in nature and should not influence the final adjudication of the case.
The ED had challenged the High Court's decision, questioning its finding that the agency had not strictly followed the procedure for communicating the grounds of arrest.

Additional Solicitor General SV Raju, appearing for the ED, told the Supreme Court that the grounds of arrest had been supplied to Khan and argued that the High Court had made adverse observations without giving the agency adequate opportunity to respond.
However, the bench refused to set aside the interim relief.
Senior advocate Kapil Sibal appeared for Khan.
Why did the Allahabad High Court grant interim bail?
The Allahabad High Court granted Khan interim bail on November 17 after examining the circumstances of his arrest on October 31.
It was prima facie of the view that the ED had not strictly complied with the safeguards under Article 22(1) of the Constitution and Section 19 of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).
Article 22(1) protects an arrested person by requiring that they be informed of the grounds of arrest and be allowed to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of their choice.

stories.headline: Amit Shah inaugurates key anti-terror conference; deliberations to focus on cross-border terrorism
stories.title: Amit Shah inaugurates key anti-terror conference; deliberations to focus on cross-border terrorism
stories.summary: New Delhi, Nov 19: Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Thursday inaugurated a two-day key anti-terror conference, which will deliberate on "cross-border terrorism" besides the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges, among others. Held annually, the conference has steadily grown into a significant gathering of operational forces, agencies working in the field of counter-terrorism, and experts from the technical, legal and forensic domains. It offers the agencies/forces an opportunity to collectively examine matters that have bearing on national security and the threats arising from terrorism. In keeping with the 'whole of government approach', the conference places particular emphasis on fostering synergy among all stakeholders. It seeks to establish formal as well as informal channels that enable coordinated and concerted action against terrorism. The conference also aims at contributing substantive inputs towards the formulation of future policy, a statement issued by the Home Ministry has said. The conference sessions will address a range of subjects, including obtaining evidence from foreign jurisdictions, the application of digital forensics and data analysis in counter-terrorism investigations, and the effective management of trials, it said. Sessions will also cover countering radicalisation and emerging hybrid threats to national security. "Further sessions will examine the tools, techniques and case experiences involved in disrupting terror financing networks, as well as the development of future-ready counter-terrorism strategies and the strengthening of institutional capacities to meet emerging national security challenges," said the statement issued on Wednesday. The conference is being organised by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) as a part of a continued effort to bolster the nation's collective response to terrorism. This year's conference deliberates on the theme "cross-border terrorism", it said. The conference will also host a capacity-building training programme for state police personnel and practising professionals. The programme has been designed to equip participants in several areas. These include applying the new criminal laws in terror investigations, using digital evidence in prosecution, and trial strategy and management. "The programme will also cover special provisions relating to the investigation of terror cases, common challenges posed by the defence, the protection of witnesses, and the initiatives taken by the government to improve prosecution," the statement said. Over the two days, the deliberations will enable law enforcement agencies to share their experiences, highlight good practices in handling counter-terrorism matters, and draw upon lessons learnt from terror investigations. The conference is being attended by senior police officers of states and Union Territories, officers of central agencies and departments dealing with counter-terrorism, and experts from allied fields including law, forensics and technology.
